note: Small MDC camp on the east shore of the 27-acre lake: a gravel loop with a few short gravel spurs under scattered hardwoods, next to the boat-ramp lot, with a privy. The west spurs end 20-30 m from the water across mown ground. No water. Gravel road in. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: a built gravel camping loop with spurs (map camping symbol + GIS point), not a lot - stays. Phone matches. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Lakeview at least; LAKEFRONT upgrade lead reported, not written. Pin on the loop, no move.
flags: LOT RULE - STAYS (built camp): the page lists 'Individual Campsites' (description: 'boat ramp and picnic areas'); the 7/15/2020 map legend has 'Primitive Camping' and draws the symbol north of the north Parking Lot on the east shore, with a Privy symbol beside it; GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point at 39.19254,-92.20632. Imagery (leaf-off, 0.14 m/px) shows a real camp there: a gravel loop about 60 m across entered from the area road, with three or four short gravel spurs and a cross lane, a picnic table on one spur, and a tent and vehicles on the grass at its south side; the gravel boat-ramp lot adjoins it on the south-west (trucks with boat trailers parked). No brochure PDF on the page, so no site count or campsite season is published; none written.

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview; LAKEFRONT LEAD, not written): Tri-City Community Lake is 27 acres (page), so not a pond. The loop's north lane ends about 19 m from the shore and the west spur (the one the pin is beside) ends about 30 m from it; the ground between is mown grass under scattered bare hardwoods down to a low bank, with no road, lot or built day-use feature between (the ramp and its lot are south of the loop). The east spurs are 45-60 m back behind the west ones. So two spur ends sit on open ground within 30 m of the water with nothing between: that reads as lakefront for those two, lakeview for the rest. Left at lakeview (leaf-off imagery only, no campsite photos, and MDC does not say which gravel is a campsite) - an upgrade lead for a human look, not a change.
PIN: stored 39.19254,-92.20632 (GIS point) is on the grass about 3 m from the west spur. No move.
ACCESS: gravel Tri-City Road, then about 150 m of gravel area road; no ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording. Spurs look 10-15 m long; site length is not published.
PHONE: stored 573-815-7900 matches the page's 'For more information call (573) 815-7900'.
Nothing else in the database within 3 km. No split (one camp).
